Clara — thanks for the clear list. I put together an initial unified integration checklist (attached) and sketched owners/timing below. High level answers first, then a proposed POC cadence.

Quick answers:
- SDKs: Our Node + Python SDKs both support streaming with prefix/KV cache helpers. For microservice architectures we recommend the long-lived KV cache on a Redis instance colocated with service cluster (we include sample code in the checklist).
- Auth: For POC you can start with short-lived API keys scoped per environment. For production we recommend OAuth with JWKS + KMS for key wrapping. We will send a short doc for KMS integration with examples for AWS KMS and GCP.
- Routing: We have routing policies you can declare in YAML: priority by region, then by latency SLO, then fallback by cost tier. I included one sample policy (us-west primary, eu fallback, then 'economy' model).
- Structured output / tool-calling: We recommend using the runtime's function-calling schema with strict JSON schema validation on the server side. There is also a helper lib in the SDK for type-safe bindings.
- Embeddings / rerankers: For PHI/clinical notes we recommend running embeddings in your VPC/private deployment (Redwood Private) with a matched, medically-tuned embedding model (we suggested two options in the checklist). For on-prem storage, Vector DBs we commonly see: Milvus (self-hosted), or FAISS when tight control required.

Proposed immediate owners & timeline (POC: 6 weeks):
- Week 0: Kickoff + account provisioning (Owner: Sean)
- Week 1: SDK onboarding + streaming example (Owner: Nebula Eng: Alex / Redwood: SDK eng)
- Week 2: Auth proof-of-concept (short-lived API keys -> KMS demo) (Owner: Marissa)
- Week 3-4: Embeddings + reranker eval on sample corpus (Owner: Nebula Search Eng)
- Week 5: Integrate function-calling path + end-to-end test (Owner: Nebula Eng + Sean)
- Week 6: Red-team prompt injection dry run + governance handoff (Owner: Redwood Security)

Next steps I can take this week:
1) Share the attached checklist + prompt governance starter workbook (attached).
2) Kickoff call — propose Wed 9/2 at 10:00am PT.

Let me know if that works and I’ll send calendar invite.

Alex / Clara — quick answers ahead of the kickoff and action items (final message).

Embeddings in Private: The medically-tuned embedding variants are available for Private deployments in the current catalog (model ids referenced in the checklist under the 'Private supported models' tab). For the POC we can stage a small private model image to your VPC so you can run locally.

Function-calling validation patterns: Two practical options we use in the field:
- Runtime JSON Schema validation (post-return): enforce strict contract server-side, fail-safe mapping for unknown enum values. Preferred when you can control the reconciliation service and want deterministic handling.
- Prompt-driven constraining + classifier gate: use a classifier or token-level detector to reject or map unexpected values before hitting the reconciliation pipeline. This is useful when you can’t change the downstream service quickly.

Prompt governance / injection mitigations (summary from starter workbook):
- Version prompts: store system prompts as versioned artifacts in your repository with small numeric semver and change notes. Track prompt-to-eval mappings so every prompt change has a small regression test.
- Input sanitization: canonicalize and escape user-provided content before feeding to model; use blocklists for known unsafe patterns.
- Red-teaming: run adversarial prompt sets during Week 5 (owner: Redwood Security). We recommend a 2-stage red-team: automated fuzzy mutations + human review on high-risk intents.
- Emergency rollback: keep previous prompt versions pinned to a fallback policy so you can roll back within minutes.
